title: Miridian - POC weekly latency & throughput review
summary: Weekly POC sync covering lab benchmark deltas vs the customer's incumbent provider. Redwood showed lower median token latency and similar throughput under steady load but higher 95th percentile on one traffic pattern; discussed batching, quantization tradeoffs, and KV/prefix caching. Agreed to run tail latency sweeps, share config/benchmark sheet, and schedule a deeper routing/quantization deep-dive next week.
action_items: Samir Patel: run 95th-percentile tail sweep with 128-token prompts and p95/p99 outputs - due 2026-12-04
Ben Carter: share benchmark spreadsheet, raw perf logs, and config dump link - due 2026-12-02
Priya Nair: provide representative traffic CSV (token distribution + arrival pattern) - due 2026-12-03
Jia Nguyen: prepare a short demo of KV-prefetch and prefix caching impact - due 2026-12-07
next_steps: Run tail-latency sweep (Samir) and report p95/p99 for 64/128 token scenarios
Redwood to share benchmark workbook and runbook link
Schedule routing/quantization deep-dive (60m) with Miridian infra and SRE - propose slots for next Tue/Wed
Customer to confirm target SLA and acceptable cost delta vs incumbent
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time (UTC): 14:30
Duration: 58 min
Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Miridian Head of ML), Luca Morales (Miridian SRE), Denise Kim (CTO), Omar Ruiz (Perf Eng)

Auto-generated Summary:
- Quick readout of this week's bench: median token latency down ~22% vs incumbent on standard conv prompts; steady-state throughput comparable; p95 regression on bursty random-access pattern observed.
- Discussed mitigation: smaller batching windows for tail traffic, KV prefix caching, quantize profile change for large context sequences.
- Agreed action items and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ben Carter: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we, uh, have about 55 minutes, want to make sure we get through the bench highlights and then the tuning asks. Priya, Denise, you there?
[00:10] Priya Nair: Yep, hi. thanks. we got Luca and Omar on too.
[00:15] Luca Morales: hey all. sorry running a tiny bit late, all good now.
[00:20] Ben Carter: great. quick agenda: one, bench delta vs your current provider; two, triage the p95 issue on bursty traffic; three, next steps and runbook. Samir will jump into the numbers.
[00:35] Samir Patel: ok so to summarize the lab run we did across three traffic patterns - conversational short prompts (avg 32 tokens), long context synth (avg 256 tokens), and random-access burst (spiky arrivals) - median token latency for conv was 18ms for us vs 23ms incumbent, so roughly 22% improvement on median. throughput under steady load at 200 concurrent reqs stayed within 5% of their baseline.
[01:03] Omar Ruiz: wait, 18 milliseconds per token? that seems optimistic, can you confirm the tokenization and measurement points? are we measuring server-side completion to first token or end-to-end?
[01:18] Samir Patel: good call — we measure server-side first-token latency plus time to generate tokens; for these runs we used a 1-token sample at a time to approximate per-token latency. there might be a small discrepancy versus your end-to-end since network egress from their infra was not identical.
[01:33] Priya Nair: and p95? where are we on tail numbers, because that's our main user pain.
[01:38] Samir Patel: yeah so here's the interesting bit — on conv and long context the p95 is about 1.8x median, similar to incumbent. but on the random-access burst pattern p95 increased to about 3.2x median which is higher than the incumbent's p95 for that pattern.
[01:58] Denise Kim: can you explain why that pattern spikes? is it scheduling? batching? some cache miss?
[02:05] Samir Patel: likely a mix. our runtime tries to batch aggressively to improve throughput — during bursts batches grow unpredictably which delays early requests behind the batch window. also KV cache misses show up when the access pattern jumps between many small contexts.
[02:23] Ben Carter: so two levers — reduce batching window for identified bursty routes, or apply per-route bypass to keep latency tight; second is pre-warming or prefix caching. Jia, did you capture the KV profiling?
[02:36] Jia Nguyen: yes, we logged the cache hit ratios during the spike and you can see hit rates drop from ~86% baseline to ~47% during the random-access runs. the prefetch heuristic we used is pretty conservative so we can tune it.
[02:50] Luca Morales: ok that explains a lot. our traffic does a fair bit of shard hopping so prefix cache hits will be low unless you prefetch aggressively which has cost implications.
[03:02] Samir Patel: exactly — there's a cost/latency tradeoff. we recommended a moderate prefetch for these endpoints, or you can set a route-level policy: low-latency route with smaller batch size + no prefetch for interactive support, and throughput-optimized route for background tasks.
[03:21] Priya Nair: what's the expected unit cost delta if we choose the low-latency route? ballpark percent.
[03:27] Ben Carter: rough ballpark from our bench: low-latency mode tends to raise token-unit compute by 8-15% vs throughput mode, but reduces p95 by 20-40% depending on prompt length. we'll attach the cost model in the workbook.
[03:40] Omar Ruiz: are you seeing any quantization-induced quality regression for long contexts when you switch to 4-bit profiles?
[03:47] Samir Patel: in our A/B we observed negligible quality drift for most prompts at q4_0 per our eval set, but long-context single-token accuracy had slight regressions in 2 of 400 queries — we flagged those. we can run a more targeted eval with your prompts.
[04:00] Denise Kim: security/regulatory quick check — we need SOC2 artifact and audit logs for the dedicated slots. did you send that previously?
[04:08] Ben Carter: yes we uploaded a SOC 2 summary, and can provide a deeper artifact pack for enterprise customers. I'll re-share the link to the security dossier in the notes.
[04:18] Priya Nair: please include the KMS/HSM integration notes because our compliance team will grill that.
[04:23] Ben Carter: noted.
[04:25] Samir Patel: back to performance — one experiment we didn't run yet at scale is the 95th/99th tail sweep across 64/128 tokens using mixed arrival distributions. that will show if the p95 spike persists when you control batch windows more aggressively.
[04:40] Priya Nair: yes please do that. also send the raw perf logs, not just aggregates — our SRE team likes to look at per-request traces.
[04:48] Ben Carter: we'll share a link to a downloadable workbook and raw logs.
[04:52] Jia Nguyen: quick demo note — we found that enabling prefix prefetch for the top 10 keys reduced the miss chatter and cut median for long-context by ~12%, though it raised token compute slightly. can demo during the deep-dive.
[05:07] Luca Morales: would be helpful to see the prefetch tradeoff numbers so we can quantify cost impact to our budget owner.
[05:12] Ben Carter: absolutely. we'll add cost columns.
[05:15] Omar Ruiz: small thing — in your previous email the routing fallback was named Triton-Compat, is that the same as your compatibility mode or a different path? we want to avoid confusing names with the incumbent.
[05:27] Samir Patel: ah yeah, sorry the name is internal shorthand. It's a compatibility fallback that routes to smaller quantized variants; we'll rename it to "compat-fallback" in docs to avoid confusion.
[05:37] Denise Kim: ok about the dedicated capacity — if we go that route, what are the lead times and do you support air-gapped on-prem?
[05:44] Ben Carter: Dedicated slots typically 4-6 weeks depending on region and capacity, on-prem (air-gapped) is supported but it's a separate package and security review — we can start that conversation in parallel.
[05:55] Priya Nair: timeline wise, we want a pilot decision within 3 weeks. does that align with your next-run deliverables?
[06:02] Ben Carter: yes, if we complete the tail-sweep and you review the workbook early next week we can decide by 2026-12-18.
[06:10] Jia Nguyen: action item recap in the doc as well.
[06:15] Ben Carter: any other sticking points?
[06:18] Omar Ruiz: minor — please include the exact model versions and kernel/quant flags you used; we've seen variance between minor builds.
[06:25] Samir Patel: will do, we'll include the model sha and runtime kernel version in the artifact pack.
[06:30] Priya Nair: one more question on routing: can Redwood do per-customer route weighting so we split 10% traffic to the new path for canary?
[06:38] Ben Carter: yes we support canary splits, per-route percentage, and automatic rollback on error spikes. we'll include the rollout snippet in the runbook.
[06:46] Luca Morales: great. also, do you provide token-level cost breakdowns per request in the analytics?
[06:52] Ben Carter: yep, per-request token accounting with breakdown by model, quant profile, and kernel selection.
[06:58] Priya Nair: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:01] Ben Carter: ok we're at about 30 minutes in; we've covered the core. let's quickly confirm owners. Samir, you'll run the tail sweep, Ben will share the workbook, Priya will push us the traffic CSV. Jia will prep the small demo.
[07:18] Priya Nair: confirmed.
[07:20] Samir Patel: confirmed.
[07:22] Ben Carter: cool — we'll aim to have the workbook and logs out within 48 hours.
[07:27] Denise Kim: thanks, one last ask — can you include a short note on cost/latency for low-latency route vs throughput route per 1M tokens? we need that for finance.
[07:35] Ben Carter: yes we'll include a per-million token estimate.
[07:38] Priya Nair: ok thanks everyone.
[07:41] Ben Carter: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with links and propose times for the deep-dive.
[07:46] (call ends)
